title: Explorer Assessment

beats.narrativeText: There's no written test waiting for the learner this time — instead, Explorer Academy hands them a completely new investigation, with nothing about it explained in advance.
No step-by-step guidance is coming this time, and none is meant to. That absence is the point of the assessment, not an oversight.
The learner investigates the unfamiliar problem and plans their own approach, the same way they now do without thinking twice about it.
Collecting the evidence reveals something the learner might not have expected: just how naturally they now do the things that once needed Atlas's guidance.
The learner must justify every decision and explain their reasoning as they go — not just produce an answer, but be able to defend how they got there.
The learner presents their conclusions. What Explorer Academy is watching for isn't a perfect answer — it's the habits of an Explorer, on full display.
The learner reflects on how differently they think now compared to Mission 1 — back when an Explorer Journal was a brand new idea, not a habit.
Explorer Academy was never evaluating facts memorised along the way — it was watching how the learner thinks. And on that measure, they've just shown they're ready for full membership.

activities.title: Investigate an Unfamiliar Problem
activities.storyContext: The Academy presents the learner with a completely new investigation, with no step-by-step guidance — the same way real investigations actually start.
activities.instructions: Begin investigating the unfamiliar problem the Academy has presented, in whatever way makes sense to you first.
activities.output: Initial notes on the unfamiliar problem.

activities.title: Plan Your Approach
activities.storyContext: The learner chooses how to approach the problem and selects whatever methods actually fit it, rather than a prescribed set.
activities.instructions: Plan how you will approach the investigation and which methods you will use, before diving into collecting evidence.

activities.title: Collect Evidence
activities.storyContext: A strong conclusion needs strong evidence — the same standard every investigation this campaign has held you to.
activities.instructions: Follow your plan and collect evidence for your investigation, adjusting the plan if it isn't working rather than forcing it.

activities.title: Justify Decisions
activities.storyContext: Explorer Academy values reasoning throughout an investigation, not just a tidy explanation bolted on at the end.
activities.instructions: Explain the reasoning behind the decisions you made during your investigation, as you made them, not just how it turned out.
activities.output: A written justification of your investigative decisions.

activities.title: Present Conclusions
activities.storyContext: The emphasis is not on a perfect answer, but on demonstrating the habits of an Explorer — the same habits Explorer Academy noticed all the way back in Mission 1.
activities.instructions: Present your conclusions and explain how you reached them, clearly enough that someone else could follow your thinking.

activities.title: Identify Improvements
activities.storyContext: Even a strong investigation can always be improved.
activities.instructions: Identify improvements that could strengthen your investigation.

activities.title: How Different Experts Investigate
activities.storyContext: Different kinds of experts might approach the same problem in very different ways.
activities.instructions: Consider how different experts might investigate the same problem in different ways.
activities.output: None required — this is an open discussion.

prompts: How did you decide which methods to use for a problem with no instructions, and how is that different from how you'd have approached it back in Mission 1?

discussionPoints: How did you decide where to start with no instructions?
What are you most proud of in how you approached this investigation?
parentGuide.preparation: No special preparation required — this investigation is designed to be open-ended.
parentGuide.assessment: Look for a clearly explained approach and reasoning, not just a final answer — the process matters more than a single correct result.

completionCriteria: An unfamiliar problem investigated, evidence collected, decisions justified, and conclusions presented.
